function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. Here’s a quick overview of key figures who helped uncover its nature:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | First recorded observations of static electricity (rubber rubbed with fur). |
| **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | Coined the term *electricus* and distinguished between magnetism and static electricity. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Conducted the famous kite experiment, proving that lightning is electrical. |
| **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile, the first chemical battery, providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying the groundwork for electric generators. |
| **James Clerk Maxwell** (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single theory of electromagnetism. |

So while many scientists contributed to our understanding of electricity, it was not “discovered” by a single individual.
